newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen up on Pacific Intertie news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen up on Pacific Intertie news.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open higher Friday amid news of the capacity on the Pacific Intertie transmission system could be reduced on July 1.

In over-the-counter activity, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $27.50-27.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Thursday's settlement at $26.76, while July California-Oregon Border (COB) at $17.50-18.00 against yesterday's close at $17.08.
Transmission capacity on the intertie will likely fall in early July to 6,300 megawatts (MW), compared with the current limit of 7,200 MW, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) told Reuters Thursday.
In the meantime, a Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is expected to propose next week a summertime rating for the intertie of 6,900 MW.
"That's causing some concern in the market," said a West Coast electricity dealer.
The complex managed to finish modestly higher yesterday despite softer spot West cash prices due to forecasts of seasonal weather and increasing supply.
Meterologists called for temperatures across the West next week to run near to slightly above-normal with precipitation averaging near to above-normal.
Main cities along the West Coast from Seattle down to San Diego would see readings in the 70s F, while those in the interior Southwest such as Phoenix and Tucson would experience weather in the 90s.
More than 2,500 megawatts of generation are expected to return to service by next week.

Several West coal-fired power units began restarting yesterday: a 450 MW San Juan unit in New Mexico, a 300 MW Reid Gardner unit in Nevada, a 190 MW Hayden unit in Colorado and a 670 MW Centralia unit in Washington.
Furthermore, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was expected to resume power production next week, ahead of the original schedule.
Meanwhile, a 875 MW unit at the Intermountain coal-fired power plant in Utah is said to shut today through Sunday to repair a tube leak.
Separately, scheduled maintenance on the Pacific Intertie which began yesterday is scheduled to be completed today.
Market sources said reduction on the transmission system which moves power from the Northwest to southern California was having minimal impact on spot prices.
